A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical multi-armed bandit study. Their main text, equations, algorithms, figure and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved from Section 4.3 to Appendix C.5.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical bounds, algorithm analyses and proofs. Neither its main text nor its appendices report original experiments, simulations or data analyses.

after.justification: V2 remains entirely theoretical. Its main text and appendices contain no original experimental, simulation, user-study or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: The Bernoulli bandit model and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same inputs, randomization, thresholds, boosting and stopping rules. Remark 1.2 adds context about obtaining success-probability guarantees using existing algorithms, without revising the proposed procedures.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical datasets or evaluated task collections. The interactive, non-interactive and expected-stopping-time bandit settings are theoretical settings already present in v1.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. V2's additional references to median elimination, knowledge gradient and other methods are literature discussion, not newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version contains empirical evaluation protocols. Making the large-time saturation regime explicit in v2 does not change experimental budgets, metrics or testing procedures.

E4.justification: No empirical ablations or robustness tests are added or removed. The analytical counterexamples in Section 4.1, separation construction in Section 4.2 and corresponding appendix analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The probability and concentration bounds are theoretical rather than empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added, removed or revised. The central success-probability and information-growth rates remain the same; large-time saturation, newly foregrounded in v2, was already stated in v1's introduction.

T1.justification: V1 Section 4.3 incorrectly states that I*(t,E) is non-increasing in t; v2 Appendix C.5 corrects this to I*(t,E)/t. Theorem 1.1 and related bounds also explicitly incorporate saturation already noted in v1. The principal proofs and rates remain intact.

C1.justification: The information-growth and learning–information separation claims are retained. V2 modestly narrows contribution positioning by explicitly acknowledging in Remark 1.2 and Figure 1 that success-probability achievability is also available through existing algorithms.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly limits its algorithms to theoretical case-study purposes and disclaims recommending them for general settings. Remark 1.2 also distinguishes known success-probability guarantees from the unresolved information guarantees of the cited alternative. The stopping-time conjecture and its obstacle are retained after relocation.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, thresholds and algorithmic budgets are unchanged. Neither version supplies implementation environments, hardware measurements or code/data access information, and v2 adds no such disclosures.

R1.justification: V2 expands discussion of best-arm identification and ridge bandits, adding references such as Even-Dar et al., Mannor and Tsitsiklis, Frazier and Powell, and additional fixed-budget work. Its explicit recognition of prior success-probability achievability refines novelty attribution without replacing the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 expands the introductory motivation, adds Remark 1.2 and notation clarifications, edits wording and an author affiliation, and moves the detailed stopping-time conjecture discussion into Appendix C.5. The abstract and overall section sequence remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 retains its dependency structure but fades the success-probability achievability node and expands its caption to acknowledge prior work. Definitions are combined into one display, Theorem 1.1 uses expanded piecewise displays, and algorithm placement and pagination change. No new figures or tables appear.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects the stopping-time monotonicity statement, clarifies the algorithms' applicability limits and gives more precise credit for existing achievability results. The explicit saturation presentation also improves accessibility. These are useful, limited improvements; the principal algorithms, bounds and proofs remain substantially unchanged.
